meta.title: deep-layer attention pruning for visual grounding

units.text: Visual token pruning is essential for efficient vision-language model inference, yet existing attention-based methods either fail catastrophically on spatially-sensitive tasks or require offline calibration data.
units.s2: does it help understanding, checking, reproducing or reading limits?

units.text: We present a simple solution: use attention from deeper layers.
units.s2: does it help understanding, checking, reproducing or reading limits?

units.text: While prior methods like D [math] Pruner extract attention from shallow layers (L2) and apply offline debiasing, we show that attention at layer 12 of InternVL2.5-8B is semantically rich enough to directly guide token selection without any debiasing.
